name: Herod the Great and the children of Bethlehem
charge: Slaying all the male children of Bethlehem from two years old and under
summary: Herod was set over Judea by Rome and was an Edomite, not of Israel, and when the wise men asked after the one born King of the Jews he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. He got the birthplace out of the chief priests, enquired privately after the time of the star, and sent the wise men to search under a pretence that he also wished to worship. When they did not come back he was exceeding wroth and slew all the children in Bethlehem and its coasts from two years old and under. Matthew reports his death and no sentence explaining it, and joins the mourning to Jeremiah’s word about Rachel.
offenseFull: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, and wise men came from the east to Jerusalem asking where he was that is born King of the Jews, and when Herod heard it he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him (Matthew 2:1-3). The study notes press the reason: Herod was set up as king over Judea by Rome, and he was an Edomite, not of Israel. If the messiah were coming to save all nations, there would be nothing in his birth to trouble a ruler of the nations. He is troubled because the messiah coming to Israel means judgment on those who hold Israel down.

The class traces the house behind the name. Antipater, a native of Idumea, founded the Herodian dynasty and was the father of Herod; he rose under the later Hasmonean kings, became a client of Pompey, was made chief minister of Judea by Julius Caesar, and set his sons over Jerusalem and Galilee. That family had converted to Judaism, so they were schooled in the customs and prophecies of Israel without being of Israel, and the Herodians of the gospels were that same stock, the ones spoken of as saying they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan (Revelation 2:9). Herod married a Hasmonean princess to give himself a claim and then killed her, and destroyed the old priestly line and the men who might have been rivals. The history class puts it sharply: this is the man who now says he also wishes to worship the child.

He gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and demanded of them where Christ should be born, and they answered at once out of the prophet, Bethlehem of Judea (Matthew 2:4-6; Micah 5:2). They knew the scriptures concerning the messiah, and the same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them; Israel obtained not that which he sought for, and the rest were blinded (Romans 11:7-10). Then Herod called the wise men privily, enquired what time the star appeared, and sent them to Bethlehem to search for the young child and bring him word, saying that he would come and worship also (Matthew 2:7-8). What he did next showed what he had in mind.

Being warned of God in a dream, they departed into their own country another way (Matthew 2:12); and when Herod saw that he was mocked of the wise men, he was exceeding wroth, and sent forth and slew all the children in Bethlehem and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired (Matthew 2:16). The history class explains the age he chose: the star had been standing out about two years, so he killed every child of two years and under in hope that the messiah was among them; that is why Luke shows an infant and Matthew a child already walking. The study notes set the pattern beside Egypt, where the ruler charged that every son born be cast into the river, the same attempt to cut off a deliverer before he could rise (Exodus 1:22), and beside the great red dragon standing before the woman ready to be delivered, to devour her child as soon as it was born (Revelation 12:3-4), that dragon being the old serpent, the Devil and Satan (Revelation 12:9), and red the colour Esau was born (Genesis 25:25).
judgmentFull: The design failed. The angel had already told Joseph to take the young child and his mother into Egypt, and he departed by night and remained there until the death of Herod, so that the prophet’s word, that God called his son out of Egypt, was fulfilled (Matthew 2:13-15; Hosea 11:1). When Herod was dead the angel told Joseph to return to the land of Israel, because they were dead which sought the young child’s life (Matthew 2:19-20). Matthew reports the death of the king and nothing of the manner of it, and he pronounces no separate sentence upon him.

What Matthew does set down is the mourning, written beforehand by Jeremiah: a voice heard in Ramah, lamentation and weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they were not (Matthew 2:17-18; Jeremiah 31:15). The ruler died and the promised child lived. The children of Bethlehem were still murdered, and neither the failure of the plot nor the fulfilling of the prophecy touches the guilt of the hand that shed their blood; hands that shed innocent blood are among the things the Lord hates (Proverbs 6:16-17), and the man that takes reward to slay an innocent person is under the curse pronounced before all the people (Deuteronomy 27:25).

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Those guilty of murder are to be put to death.
Rulers are not to be a terror to good behavior, but rather to the wicked and evil doers.
It is an abomination for a civil ruler to commit wickedness, for his office is established on righteousness.

text.text: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,
Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.
When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.
And when he had gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people together, he demanded of them where Christ should be born.
And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet,
And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.

But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded
(According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.
And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them:
Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.
Then Herod, when he had privily called the wise men, enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared.
And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said, Go and search diligently for the young child; and when ye have found him, bring me word again, that I may come and worship him also.
And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.

Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.
And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.

And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.
And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.
And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.

And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:
And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.
When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
Saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young child’s life.
Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying,
In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
Thus saith the Lord; A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rahel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not.
These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:
A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.
